Deviation from contracts.md 2.4 (tighter, recorded in tasks/todo.md): catalog writes (products, packaging_types, price_list_items, product_costs) require fn_has_module('catalog') AND fn_user_role() IN ('owner','accountant'). Without it the seed sales/ops users (who hold catalog for the read-only Products list) could still set floor_price = 1 (replay showed UPDATE 12), voiding the 0005 floor guard. contracts.md is read-only for me; the contract owner should add one line.

Residual by contract design: a non-owner who holds the users module may demote or deactivate an owner as long as another active owner remains (only granting 'owner' and removing the last owner are refused). Tightening to 'only owners touch owners' would make last_owner unreachable and needs a contract change.

0001 still runs GRANT ALL ON ALL TABLES/ROUTINES and FOR ALL policies on every re-run; the end state is correct only because 0003 always runs after it. Any tool that applies 0001 alone against a live DB briefly re-opens the holes (Dev-1 file).

On hosted Supabase, global (non-schema) default privileges for role postgres may still grant TRUNCATE to anon/authenticated on tables created by 0004-0006; 0003 fixes the per-schema defaults and all existing tables, and ci:tenant-check will flag anything that slips through. Re-run ci:tenant-check against the hosted DB after Sprint B.
Seed owner (supabase/seed/01_core.sql, Dev-1) still holds the audit module, so the demo owner sees 119 audit rows; contracts section 8 says audit/documents/reports are removed from the demo owner.
notes_for_qa: Apply order matters: 0000, 0001, 0002 then 0003. scripts/seed.ts and tests/helpers/db.ts do this; tests apply all files inside one transaction under pg_advisory_xact_lock(73003) so parallel test files never see a half-applied state.

Impersonation in SQL: SET ROLE authenticated; SELECT set_config('request.jwt.claim.sub', '<user uuid>', false); back with RESET ROLE and set_config(...,'',false) (tests/helpers/db.ts actAs/resetRole). Session overrides app.current_org / app.override_module_check are ignored for authenticated/anon/authenticator and honoured only when connected as postgres (the rls test uses that to generate codes).

Why the GUC guard is not literally current_user: inside a SECURITY DEFINER function current_user is always the owner (postgres); the SET ROLE value is read via current_setting('role') (verified: 'authenticated' inside a definer under SET ROLE, 'none' otherwise), falling back to session_user.

Error codes raised by fn_set_user_access / fn_set_user_active: self_change, role_not_allowed, not_found -> SQLSTATE 42501; last_owner, bad_payload -> SQLSTATE P0001 (contract silent on the last two; chosen so permission failures and rule failures are distinguishable). fn_require_module keeps 'Access denied: module X is required' (42501).

fn_has_module(NULL) and any internal error -> false (never raises). fn_user_role() -> NULL without an active profile. product_costs SELECT needs owner/accountant; v_product_costs follows that (sales: 0 rows). audit_log SELECT needs org + audit module; business_settings snapshots have no bank_details key; product_costs rows are never audited.
